transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble at work lately. When people ask me a simple question... like when a ring repair will be ready... my answer just sort of wanders. I start out on invoices, and then somehow I'm talking about garden soil, or mortgage papers. I can see them losing me. So... that's why I came in.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

I... well, sometimes. Just when the shop is really quiet. I might hear... someone muttering my name. Like a woman's voice, coming from the polishing room. Or I'll smell burning metal, even though the torches are off. It feels real enough that I usually go check... but, that's all.
Have you been experiencing any periods where your mood feels unusually high, expansive, or extremely low for days or weeks at a time?

No... not high. Just... low, I suppose. Most mornings I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness. It's just... like the color has drained out of the house before I even get to the shop. It's been like that for a while.
When you experience this heavy sadness, does it happen at the same time as you hear the voices, or do you feel this way even when the voices are not present?

I suppose... yes. During the worst months, it was all at once. The sadness, and just... losing interest in things. It was happening right at the same time I kept hearing my name in the shop. And... well, I was also sure the customers were only coming in to check up on our payments. So... yes, they happened together.

Looking back at the entire time you have dealt with these voices and thoughts, would you say you have felt this heavy sadness for most of that time, or have there been long periods where the voices were present but your mood was actually fine?

I suppose... most of the time. There aren't really long periods where I feel fine. For most of the time this has all been going on, that bleak mood is just... there. Along with not sleeping much, and having no real appetite. And... just feeling guilty about things. It's been a part of my daily life, mostly. Not just a brief bad week here or there.
Have there ever been at least two weeks where you felt stable or even-keeled in your mood, but you were still hearing those voices or feeling that people were checking up on your payments?

Well... yes, I suppose. There was a time, before the sadness really took hold. I was still running my jewelry classes, still keeping up with the garden. I felt... alright, mood-wise. But for several weeks during that time, I kept hearing these... noises coming from the polishing room. And I couldn't shake the feeling that the customers were watching the business. So... yes, there was a stretch like that.

When you are convinced that the customers are coming in to check on your payments, do you have any evidence or logical explanation for why they would be doing that, or does it just feel like a fact you know to be true?

I don't really have... proof, I guess. I know it sounds odd. But I'm just convinced some of them are coming in to check whether I'll miss payments. They just... they ask too many questions about the new showroom. My husband says they're only being friendly, but... it doesn't feel that way. It just feels like something I know.
Does this tendency for your thoughts to wander and your speech to become disorganized happen even during those weeks when your mood feels perfectly fine?

Yes, it does. That's... actually why I came in. People will ask me a simple question, like when a ring repair will be ready, and... my answer just drifts. I'll start talking about invoices, and then somehow I'm talking about garden soil, or the mortgage papers. I can see them losing me. It happens even when I'm not feeling so down.
Aside from the voices and the belief about the customers, have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast to others, or that outside forces were controlling your movements or actions?
No... no, I haven't experienced anything like that. My thoughts are my own. And... no one is controlling me. It's just the other things I mentioned.
How long have these experiences, such as hearing the voices or feeling that customers are checking up on you, been happening to you in total?
I suppose... it's been a while now. The voices and... the worries about the customers, and the odd smells... I think it all started around a year and eight months ago. Somewhere around there.

When your speech wanders from one topic to another, like from invoices to garden soil, do you find that you are unable to follow your own train of thought or that your words become jumbled and hard to understand?

I... I thought I just explained that. It's... they ask about a ring repair, and I end up talking about invoices and then soil and mortgage papers. I know they can't follow me. That's... that's why I'm here. I don't know if my words are jumbled, I just... I lose them.
